Pendulum_lab has experienced a real physical disturbance (vibration, thermal shock, electromagnetic interference, or equipment misalignment) on day 26 that transiently excited the system; resonance damping or environmental coupling explains the broad negative autocorrelations observed in all four streams at characteristic lags.

Pendulum_lab instrumental drift or calibration error: the instrument's transfer function or zero-point has shifted on day 26 due to thermal creep, mechanical fatigue, or electronic drift in its readout circuit; this is independent of the negative autocorrelations elsewhere.

Trial-timestamp or data-indexing artifact: trials 175–180 have been mislabeled in time, or their raw readings have been recorded but not yet corrected for a known calibration offset that applies only to day-26 data; the negative autocorrelations are byproducts of similar index or timing artifacts across all streams.

The negative autocorrelations at characteristic lags and the strong pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_obs cross-correlation are statistical false discoveries arising from multiple-comparisons bias in lag-searching; the day-26 pendulum_lab excursion is the only genuine anomaly and is unrelated to those correlations.
